surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Kantserov bags a hat trick
paras: Drew Commesso was back in an NHL net for the first time since Mar 9, 2026, and got the win. The Blackhawks scored four times in the first. Frank Nazar struck first for the Blackhawks just 35 seconds into the game, and Tyler Bertuzzi made it 2-0 on the power play a little over two minutes later. Roman Kantserov stretched the lead to 3-0 on the power play midway through the first. Dominic Toninato made it 4-0 a little over a minute later. Vancouver pulled Nikita Tolopilo after four goals and turned to Kevin Lankinen for the rest of the first. Zeev Buium got the Canucks on the board midway through the first, and Filip Chytil cut Chicago’s lead to 4-2 early in the second. Kantserov struck again midway through the period to make it 5-2 for the Blackhawks. Jake DeBrusk made it 5-3 four minutes later. Kantserov completed his hat trick on the power play midway through the third to make it 6-3 for the Blackhawks. Bertuzzi finished with a goal and two assists.
The chances were closer than the score. The Canucks hit three posts and the crossbar, and the bounces never came.

Special teams did the work: the Blackhawks scored three power-play goals on four chances and killed all five Canucks power plays. The Hawks moved to 8-14-2, still last in the Central, while the Canucks fell to 6-19-1, still last in the NHL.
